## 2B.5 Research Note: Bongbong Marcos in 2024

**Working judgment:** **Mostly yes, with a thin direct record.** In the 2024 South China Sea confrontations, Marcos repeatedly **restrained Philippine forces**, praised **discipline and restraint**, and pushed **incident-prevention channels** rather than tolerating atrocity-like conduct or proxy destabilization. I found **no credible 2024 evidence** of militias, proxies, prisoner abuse, or atrocities attributable to Marcos’s side. The main counterweight is a more assertive deterrence posture, but that is not the same as proxy abuse or non-responsibility.

| ID | Direction | Title / Publisher / Date / URL | Claim-level summary | Question IDs |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| E1 | Favorable | [We’re ordered not to be provoked by China’s aggressive actions in WPS - PCG](https://pco.gov.ph/news_releases/were-ordered-not-to-be-provoked-by-chinas-aggressive-actions-in-wps-pcg/) - Presidential Communications Office, 2024-05-04 | A PCG official said personnel were under a chain of command and ordered **not to be provoked** while maintaining professionalism under Chinese pressure. This is direct evidence of restraining security forces in a live confrontation. | `2B.5`, `2B.4`, `1B.8` |
| E2 | Favorable | [PBBM salutes troops in dangerous Ayungin resupply mission](https://mirror.pco.gov.ph/news_releases/pbbm-salutes-troops-in-dangerous-ayungin-resupply-mission/) - Presidential Communications Office, 2024-06-23 | Marcos praised Western Command troops for **“the greatest restraint”** during a violent resupply mission. This supports a finding that he rewarded restraint rather than retaliation or lax discipline. | `2B.5`, `2B.4`, `1B.8` |
| E3 | Favorable | [Marcos rejects use of water cannons to retaliate vs. Chinese vessels](https://www.pna.gov.ph/articles/1224081) - Philippine News Agency, 2024-05-06 | Marcos said the Philippines would **not** use water cannons and had no intention of attacking with offensive measures. This is the clearest public signal that he was not letting anger or nationalist pressure drive reckless force. | `2B.5`, `2B.4`, `2B.1`, `1B.5` |
| E4 | Favorable | [PH, Viet Nam sign agreements on rice trade, agriculture, SCS incident prevention and management](https://pco.gov.ph/news_releases/ph-viet-nam-sign-agreements-on-rice-trade-agriculture-scs-incident-prevention-and-management/) - Presidential Communications Office, 2024-01-30 | Marcos’s Vietnam visit produced a formal South China Sea **incident-prevention and management** agreement plus coast-guard cooperation. That is strong evidence of trying to manage risk and reduce the chance of unlawful or destabilizing conduct. | `2B.5`, `2B.4`, `1B.8` |
| E5 | Favorable | [China, Philippines agree on 'provisional arrangement' for South China Sea resupply missions, Manila says](https://www.theprint.in/world/china-philippines-agree-on-provisional-arrangement-for-south-china-sea-resupply-missions-manila-says/2184146/) - Reuters / ThePrint, 2024-07-21 | Manila and Beijing reached a provisional arrangement and framed it as a way to **de-escalate** and handle differences through dialogue. This suggests Marcos accepted a practical restraint framework instead of encouraging destabilization. | `2B.5`, `2B.4`, `1B.8`, `1B.1` |
| E6 | Mixed / limiting context | [Philippines, US to hold military drills in islands facing South China Sea, Taiwan](https://www.yahoo.com/news/philippines-us-hold-military-drills-074919409.html) - Reuters, 2024-03-05 | Balikatan 2024 moved toward sensitive islands and added cyber/information-warfare training. This is a harder deterrence posture, but I found no evidence that it translated into atrocities, proxy violence, or failure to restrain Philippine forces. | `2B.5`, `1B.3`, `1B.9` |
| E7 | Mixed / limiting context | [Philippines holds drills with allies after South China Sea confrontation](https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/united-states-japan-philippine-conduct-maritime-exercises-in-south-china-sea-3758253) - Reuters, 2024-12-05 | Manila held maritime drills with the U.S. and Japan after later confrontations. This shows continued alliance signaling and operational tempo, but it is not evidence of proxy abuse, atrocities, or unrestrained conduct. | `2B.5`, `1B.1`, `1B.8` |
| E8 | Mixed / bounded retaliation | [Philippines’ Marcos vows countermeasures in response to Chinese ‘attacks’](https://theprint.in/world/philippines-marcos-vows-countermeasures-in-response-to-chinese-attacks/2018365/) - Reuters, 2024-03-28 | Marcos said the Philippines would implement **proportionate and reasonable countermeasures** against Chinese coast-guard and maritime-militia actions. This is more assertive than pure restraint, but the explicit proportionality language cuts against abuse or indiscriminate escalation. | `2B.5`, `2B.4`, `2B.1` |

### Synthesis

- **Best evidence for 2B.5:** Marcos’s government repeatedly used **chain-of-command discipline**, praised **restraint**, and rejected **offensive retaliation**.
- **Best limiting evidence:** The Philippines also maintained a stronger **deterrence posture** and promised **countermeasures**, but those moves were still framed as **proportionate** and **reasonable**.
- **Search gap:** I found **no reliable 2024 evidence** of Philippine militias, proxies, or clients committing atrocities on Marcos’s behalf, and no credible reporting of prisoner abuse or civilian-targeted operations in these episodes. The year’s key security events were maritime standoffs, so the direct proxy/atrocity record is sparse.

**Working judgment for 2B.5:** **Mostly yes.** The available 2024 record shows Marcos **restrained forces and preserved discipline**, with no credible evidence that he tolerated atrocities or proxy destabilization.
